source.verification_required: Captured in-task for Lane A item A-02b by one direct GET of the official DCP Zoning Resolution portal HTML (sha256 pinned above) plus one GET of its print/PDF render (cross_check below). The verbatim excerpt was extracted PROGRAMMATICALLY from the raw HTML bytes (the field--name-body container) and compared character-for-character with the text drawn in the PDF (cross_check). It has NOT been re-verified by a second human reviewer, so raw_html_verified stays false and extraction_status stays extracted_draft. Which floor area is 'the maximum residential floor area permitted on the zoning lot' for a given program, whether paragraph (a) applies (special density areas, qualifying senior housing, conversions), the reach of these provisions to R6B through ZR 11-25, and every interaction with Section 23-51, any commercial overlay or special district MUST be confirmed by a qualified zoning professional (G6) before any rule citing this snapshot is published or Verified.

cross_check.method: Every page's content stream was decompressed and its text layer read in page order. After the page-2 header (section number and title, identical to the HTML <h3>) and the 'LAST AMENDED 12/5/2024' stamp, the PDF text was compared character-for-character with the HTML-derived body text, whitespace and non-breaking spaces removed on both sides. Result: identical, including every #defined term# marker and the paragraph labels (a), (1), (2), (3), (b) (the HTML draws those labels from list markup only; the PDF prints them).

verbatim_excerpt:
23-52 Maximum Number of Dwelling Units

R1 R2 R3 R4 R5 R6 R7 R8 R9 R10 R11 R12

In the districts indicated, for #buildings# containing #multiple dwelling residences#, the maximum number of #dwelling units# permitted shall be determined by dividing the maximum #residential# #floor area# permitted on the #zoning lot# by the applicable #dwelling unit# factor. The applicable #dwelling unit# factor shall be as follows:

(a) For the following types of # multiple dwelling residences#, there shall be no applicable #dwelling unit# factor:

(1) #developments# or #enlargements# of #residences# in #special density areas#;

(2) #qualifying senior housing#; or

(3) #conversions# of any non-#residential# #building#, or portion thereof, to #residences# in the #special density areas#, or outside of #special density areas#, #conversions# of #community facility# #buildings#, or portions of #buildings# containing #community facilities#, to #residences#.

(b) For all other types of # multiple dwelling residences#, the applicable #dwelling unit# factor shall be 680. Fractions equal to or greater than three-quarters resulting from this calculation shall be considered to be one #dwelling unit#.

In addition, for #zoning lots# with #residential uses# that have different #dwelling unit# factor applicability, for the purposes of calculating the maximum number of #dwelling units# permitted within #buildings#, or portions thereof, that are subject to a #dwelling unit# factor, the calculation shall exclude the #floor area# not subject to a #dwelling unit# factor before dividing by the #dwelling unit# factor. Where #floor area# in a #building# is shared by multiple #residential uses#, the #floor area# for such shared portion shall be attributed to each #residential use# proportionately, based on the percentage each #residential use# occupies of the total #floor area# of the #zoning lot#, less any shared #floor area#.
verbatim_excerpt_composition: Verbatim blocks of the section body joined by blank lines, in page order: [0] the section number and title as displayed; [1] the district list; then each paragraph. A list item is written with the label the print/PDF render prints in front of it ((a), (b), ... for the outer list; (1), (2), ... for a nested list), followed by one space; an item's heading line and its text (separated by a double line break in the HTML) are separate blocks. Defined terms (bold italic in the HTML) are written #term#, exactly as the print/PDF render writes them, inner spacing included. Runs of whitespace and non-breaking spaces are written as one space and each block is trimmed; embedded figures (images whose alt text is an editor's caption, not Resolution text) are omitted; no word was changed.

provisions.encoded_by_rule: r6b-dwelling-units: (a)(2) and (a)(1) exclude the estimate; (a)(3) is a documented limitation

notes: Captured as the governing-source candidate for the maximum number of dwelling units (ZR 23-52, City of Yes for Housing Opportunity, Last Amended 12/5/2024). Lane A item A-02b encodes the opening formula and paragraph (b) for R6B ONLY (rule r6b-dwelling-units).

Paragraph (b): factor 680; 'Fractions equal to or greater than three-quarters resulting from this calculation shall be considered to be one #dwelling unit#.' 'three-quarters' is written 0.75 in `provisions` (exact arithmetic, 3/4 = 0.75; no reading). The text counts a fraction of three-quarters or more as one dwelling unit and gives no unit for a smaller fraction, so the count is the whole number of the quotient, plus one only when its fraction is at least three-quarters (20,150 / 680 = 29.63 -> 29, the benchmark's reading).

Paragraph (a) lists three kinds of multiple dwelling residences with NO applicable factor: developments or enlargements of residences in #special density areas#; #qualifying senior housing#; and certain #conversions#. #special density areas#, #qualifying senior housing# and #conversions# are defined terms NOT captured here; whether a zoning lot or a development falls under (a) is a separate determination.

The closing paragraph (zoning lots with residential uses of different factor applicability: exclude the floor area not subject to a factor, and attribute shared floor area proportionately) is not encoded.
The HTML and the PDF both write '# multiple dwelling residences#' (a space inside the defined-term marker) in paragraphs (a) and (b); the excerpt keeps it verbatim.

DISTRICT SCOPE FOR R6B: the section's district list names 'R1 R2 R3 R4 R5 R6 R7 R8 R9 R10 R11 R12' but not R6B. ZR 11-25 (snapshot zr-11-25, 'District Designations Appended with Suffixes') states that all regulations applicable to a district designation apply to that designation appended with a suffix, except as otherwise set forth in express provisions, and that if a section lists an R4 District its provisions also apply to R4-1, R4A and R4B unless separate provisions for the suffixed districts are listed within the section. This section lists no separate provision for any suffixed R6 district, so its R6 provisions reach R6B through ZR 11-25 - a reading of 11-25, not an express naming of R6B, to be confirmed by the reviewer (Q12) together with 11-25's 'except as otherwise set forth in express provisions' caveat.
